facts.statement: Fossils of a new ceratopsian were discovered at the Liufangzi site in Jilin province, China, during excavations in 2000 and 2002.
facts.quote: In 2000 and 2002, at the Liufangzi site of China's eastern Jilin province, excavations took place during which the jaws were found of a ceratopsian new to science.

facts.statement: The species Helioceratops brachygnathus was named and described in 2009 by Jin Liyong, Chen Jun, Zan Shuqin, and Pascal Godefroit.
facts.quote: The type species Helioceratops brachygnathus was named and described in 2009 by Jin Liyong, Chen Jun, Zan Shuqin and Pascal Godefroit.

facts.statement: The known fossils include a right lower jaw dentary and a left upper jaw maxilla.
facts.quote: It is known from its holotype JLUM L0204-Y-3, a dentary of the right lower jaw. The paratype is specimen JLUM L0204-Y-4, a left maxilla of the upper jaw.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Helioceratops to be about 1.3 meters long and weigh twenty kilograms.
facts.quote: Helioceratops was a relatively small animal. In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated a length of 1.3 m (4.3 ft) and a weight of twenty kilogrammes.

facts.statement: A unique trait of Helioceratops is that its lower jaw tooth row is only 60% longer than its maximum height.
facts.quote: The ramus or horizontal branch of the dentary is deep and short, the tooth row being but 60% longer than its maximal height.

facts.statement: The lower jaw teeth of Helioceratops have up to nine secondary ridges in front of the main ridge and four behind it.
facts.quote: On the lower jaw teeth, the denticles and secondary vertical ridges are grouped asymmetrically relative to the primary ridge, with up to nine secondary ridges in front (mesial) of the main ridge and four secondary rides at it rear (distal).

facts.statement: The lower jaws of Helioceratops bear between ten and eleven teeth.
facts.quote: The lower jaws bear ten to eleven teeth.

facts.statement: Helioceratops may have shared its habitat with the dinosaur Changchunsaurus.
facts.quote: It may have shared its habitat with Changchunsaurus.

facts.statement: Helioceratops is classified within Neoceratopsia in a basal position outside the Coronosauria clade.
facts.quote: Helioceratops was placed in the Neoceratopsia, in a moderately basal position, outside of the Coronosauria.

facts.statement: Helioceratops represents one of the most derived non-Coronosauria neoceratopsians, alongside Auroraceratops and Yamaceratops.
facts.quote: Junto con Auroraceratops y Yamaceratops, Helioceratoops representa uno de los neoceratopsiano no Coronosauria más derivados.

facts.statement: Helioceratops lived in Asia during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 125 and 94 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del Cretácico, hace aproximadamente de 125 a 94 millones de años entre el Aptiense y el Cenomaniense, en lo que actualmente es Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils of Helioceratops were found in the Quantou Formation near Liufangzi in Jilin province, China.
facts.quote: Encontrado en sedimentos de la Formación Quantou cerca de la localidad de Liufangzi en la Provincia de Jilin, China.

facts.statement: Helioceratops is considered a member of the family Leptoceratopsidae.
The time range for Helioceratops is estimated from 121.4 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)
